subject: Penetration findings: attack-surface closure & supplemental evidence
messages:
From: Jared Monroe <jared.monroe@cloudwave.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com>
Cc: trust@cloudwave.com, security-assurance@cloudwave-partners.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: closure artifacts for recent penetration findings

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for sharing the pen test report last week. Our Security Assurance team has been reviewing the findings and we need a few follow-ups to close the ticket on our side before we can sign off:

- Can you provide a short remediation summary per finding (what was changed, patch versions applied, and verification steps done)? We are especially focused on the three "high" items (Admin console auth bypass, exposed internal API, and privilege escalation exploitable via 3rd-party lib).
- For the admin console, can you confirm whether the console endpoint remains accessible from the public internet or if it is now restricted to management subnets only? If restricted, a network diagram or firewall rule snapshot would be ideal.
- Do you intend to schedule a full re-test with your pen testing vendor or will you provide an internal validation + signed delta attestation? Our compliance team requires either a third-party retest (preferred for high) or a signed attestation plus logs showing verification.

Can you also share any artifacts (diff/patch, configuration changes, logs) that demonstrate the fixes? We don't need full raw logs, just the relevant slices and a checklist that maps to each finding.

Target timeline: we'd like to close by EOD 2027-04-09 if feasible. Please let me know what you can provide and when.

Thanks,
Jared Monroe
Senior Security Engineer
Cloudwave Systems

This message originated from an external sender.

From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com>
To: Jared Monroe <jared.monroe@cloudwave.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: closure artifacts for recent penetration findings

Hi Jared —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise mapping and the artifacts we're attaching. Let me know if you'd like additional detail for any specific finding.

Summary by finding (high-level):
1) Admin console auth bypass (HIGH)
   - Fix: Enforced mutual TLS for management endpoints; upgraded auth library to 4.2.1; added IP allowlist for management subnets.
   - Verification: unit + integration tests run (2027-03-28), manual auth flow validation (2027-03-30).
   - Artifact: network-segmentation-diagram.png; remediation-summary.pdf (page 2).

2) Internal API exposure (HIGH)
   - Fix: Applied route-level ACLs and moved API to internal-only VPC endpoint.
   - Verification: egress and ingress rules validated, access logs show 0 public hits since 2027-03-29.
   - Artifact: privileged-access-logs.csv; remediation-summary.pdf (page 3).

3) Privilege escalation via third-party lib (HIGH)
   - Fix: Patched vuln to lib-x v2.10; backported compensating controls and limited role mappings.
   - Verification: dependency scan + smoke tests (2027-03-27), security review sign-off 2027-04-01.
   - Artifact: fix-patches.zip; remediation-validation-checklist.xlsx.

Scope notes:
- The admin console is no longer accessible from the public internet. It is restricted to our management subnets and requires mTLS. See network-segmentation-diagram.png for details.
- We trimmed the pen-test scope to exclude legacy staging subnets that are physically air-gapped; updated-pen-test-scope.csv is attached.

Attachments included: remediation-summary.pdf, fix-patches.zip, network-segmentation-diagram.png, updated-pen-test-scope.csv

About re-test vs attestation:
- For high severity items we generally recommend an external retest. Our preferred path is to schedule a short validation window with our vendor (2–4 hours) to verify the high findings have been closed. If you require, we can provide a signed delta attestation instead, but our SOC/compliance prefers independent verification for the high items.

Proposed next steps:
1) If Cloudwave wants a full third-party retest, propose availability windows and we'll coordinate with our vendor.
2) If you accept an internal attestation + logs, we'll produce a signed delta attestation and a mapping checklist by 2027-04-05.

I'll let Vivek follow up with proposed retest windows and the temporary test access details if you want to go the vendor route.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Head of Trust & Security (Sales Operations)
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: remediation-summary.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB), fix-patches.zip (ZIP, 18 MB), network-segmentation-diagram.png (PNG, 620 KB), updated-pen-test-scope.csv (CSV, 3 KB)

From: Jared Monroe <jared.monroe@cloudwave.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.example.com>
Cc: trust@cloudwave.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: closure artifacts for recent penetration findings

Diego —

Thanks for the quick mapping and the artifacts. A couple of clarifications before we pick a path:

- Our policy is to require an independent retest for all items marked HIGH. We can accept a focused retest (only the three high findings and the admin console) rather than a full-scope retest, but it needs to be done by an external vendor.
- If a retest isn't possible within our 2027-04-09 close window, we will accept a signed delta attestation plus the logs you mentioned, but we'll mark the ticket with a conditional requirement to complete a vendor retest within 30 days.

Can Redwood provide: 1) a preferred vendor availability window for an external retest; 2) a short list of the exact test accounts/targets you recommend (URLs/IPs and temporary creds or jumpbox details) to minimize blast radius? Also send a DocuSign link for the delta attestation if you choose that route.

If you can propose an availability window today, we'll see if our team can accommodate next week.

Regards,
Jared
